🟠 [g11-protocol-allow-creep] MUST-FIX The diff adds `unset GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` to hooks/tests/lib.sh and rewrites `git clone` to `git -c protocol.file.allow=always clone` in check-hands-commit.test.sh and session-mode.test.sh. None of these is in the spec, and G11 limits existing-suite edits to (a) sourcing lib.sh, (b) scratch-dir moves, (c) the gate-off config and (d) the P0 fix. Impact: every suite that sources lib.sh now silently drops an operator- or CI-set git protocol allow-list, an uncommented security relaxation inside a containment change. It is also inconsistent: the clone in mission-terminal-rollover.test.sh did not get the same `-c`, so the workaround is either unnecessary or incomplete. Smallest remediation: delete the `unset GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` line and revert the two `-c protocol.file.allow=always` insertions; if a suite then fails solo, report it by name as the Verify clause requires instead of masking it.
🟡 [inv1-quoted-c-form-unscanned] MUST-FIX Inventory one in test-identity-guard.test.sh misses two spec-listed syntaxes. The `-c` regex requires a bare `-c<space>user.email=`, so the quoted shell form `git -c "user.email=dev@real.com"` and the JS argv form `['-c', 'user.email=dev@real.com']` are never extracted; the JS regex only handles the `'user.email', 'value'` pair. Impact: a non-G2 address in those positions passes KR5 silently, and the fixture conversion that relied on this scanner may have left offenders behind. Smallest remediation: replace the `-c` regex with one anchored on `user\.email=` that tolerates an opening quote before `user` (e.g. `/user\.email=["']?([^\s"';|&,\])]+)/g`), re-run the suite, and convert anything it newly reports to `@example.invalid`.

Not blocking: G11(a) permits this edit, and the inventory-two acceptance (every git-invoking test sources lib.sh) cannot pass without it, since these files do run git mid-line. The dispatcher should ratify the widened file set.
